guardrails.rationale: Genetic or biochemical research is planned or still uncertain.
guardrails.action: Confirm the applicable provider-country measures with the authority or partner. Review prior informed consent, mutually agreed terms, benefit-sharing terms, and any IRCC. Record why a pathway is or is not applicable.

guardrails.title: Check obligations in the research country
guardrails.rationale: Research is using genetic resources, potentially from another jurisdiction.
guardrails.action: Review the research institution’s due-diligence process and applicable user-country requirements alongside provider-country measures.

guardrails.title: Review material transfer and border requirements
guardrails.rationale: Material transfer is planned or has not been ruled out.
guardrails.action: Confirm origin and destination, recipient, material transfer terms, export/import and biosecurity requirements. If listed species are involved, check CITES applicability and any scientific exemptions.

guardrails.title: Review traditional knowledge and community terms
guardrails.rationale: Associated traditional knowledge may form part of the study.
guardrails.action: Identify knowledge holders and the applicable consent and benefit-sharing process. Agree how knowledge and sensitive metadata may be reused or shared.

guardrails.title: Review sequence-data sharing terms
guardrails.rationale: The study involves genetic or biochemical research.
guardrails.action: If sequence data will be generated or reused, review publication permissions, repository terms, and current DSI guidance. Do not infer a Cali Fund payment from sequencing alone.

guardrails.title: Record the site-review acknowledgment
guardrails.rationale: The fieldwork review process has not been acknowledged.
guardrails.action: Confirm the planned site-review process. This acknowledgment is separate from any permit or approval.

sources.title: New Zealand · Research and wildlife applications
sources.summary: DOC provides different application routes for research, collection, wildlife, and marine reserve activities.

sources.title: New Zealand · Marine reserve research
sources.summary: DOC distinguishes sampling and interference from some non-interfering observation activities. Identify the reserve and activity before reviewing permissions.

sources.title: CBD · ABS country profiles
sources.summary: Country profiles contain nationally published measures, authorities, and ABS procedures. Consult the relevant authority for the specific activity.

sources.title: CBD · Nagoya Protocol
sources.summary: A framework for access, benefit sharing, traditional knowledge, and compliance with applicable domestic measures.

sources.title: CITES · How CITES works
sources.summary: International movement of listed specimens may involve permits, certificates, and specific scientific exemptions. Verify with the relevant management authorities.

sources.title: AAUS · Scientific diving guidance
sources.summary: Use the diving oversight and approval process of the responsible institution. An acknowledgment here is not diving authorization.

sources.title: CBD · Multilateral mechanism and Cali Fund
sources.summary: Digital sequence information has a separate benefit-sharing mechanism. Review current guidance and agreed sharing terms; sequencing does not automatically create a payment obligation.
